x: Thanks to some good last lap running by Blunden, Charlton and Stan Davies we eventually ran out winners of the "Dewar" Shield with a total of 141 points, with South London 145 and Herne Hill 177.
Len Marchant kept the lead and then Stan Davies went off and running with a badly blistered foot he allowed the Surrey men to get within two seconds of him.

There was rather a gap after the first three home but the rest of the field then arrived at regular intervals with Tom Carter and Stan Davies having a desperate sprint to the finishing line, which Tom won by inches.
Stan Davies surprised most people, including himself, by winning the 440 yards, while Lionel Grimshaw was second in the 220 yards and we also had first and third in the 100.

Ruddick carried on the good work and " clocked " 14min. 48secs. to further increase our lead and with Stan Davies doing 15min. 13secs. and Len Adams 15min. 9secs., Eddie Short went off on the fifth stage with a good lead.

Jack Brown carried on the good work and gave us a lead of about sixty yards at the end of the third relay. Stan. Davies was our next runner, but despite a gallant effort he had to give way to Macoy of Aylesford who ran a very well judged race.
Frank Abberton, who we were pleased to see turning out again, had a sprint to the finishing line with Jim Bragginton, and then came Ted Stimpson followed by Stan Davies.

Ted Stimpson ran his usual dependable race and Steve Charlton also did well as did Stan Davies, our new Track Captain, and with four in the first 33 we should have gained a place, but our fifth and sixth counters were too far back and so we had to be content with finishing fourth in the team race.

Tom Carter and Stan Davies gave Steve good support and Bert Footer also qualified for a prize as the fourth member of our "A" team. It was quite like old times to see Tom and Bert going up for their "pots."
Len Bishop went next and Bowering of S.L.H. gained 26 secs. on Len but we were still leading and Stan Davies on the next leg gained a little to make the margin in our favour 42 secs.

Arthur Bruce was second in the 880 yards and Stan Davies had to run a quarter in order to gain a point for third place. Our bright "spot" was the 1 mile win of Bill Lucas in 4 min. 29 secs. and that of Les.

This was held on the same evening as the Tadworth match and our numbers suffered accordingly, but we did not do so badly, and in a five-sided contest we finished in third position. Gordon Lowers won the 100 yards and Mullen won the 220, while Stan Davies was third in the Mile and Bergvalds was second in the Shot Putt.
Bragginton did 14.38 to further increase our lead and then Len Adams returned 14.48 and when he handed over to Stan Davies the next team was not in sight.

“Judge praises Tooting runner,” these were the headlines in a local paper recently, and they referred to the fact that our track captain, Stan Davies, had assisted in apprehending a man who assaulted a young girl on Tooting Bec Common.
Basil Walden won the Club 75 yards handicap with John Smith 2nd and Eddie Lacey 3rd, while Stan Davies showed some of his old form when he won the 2 miles run off 280 yards in 9 min. 21 secs.

This was won by Stan Davies with George Stace just beating Len Rolls on the tape for second place. Bob Taylor and Stan Davies are both in hospital with chest trouble. Stan says the doctors have told him that it has nothing whatever to do with athletics and that he will be fit for action again in two years time.
Secretary welcomed Bob Taylor and Stan Davies on their return to the Club , both of whom were in hospital last year. We were also pleased to see Ron Linstead back after a spell in hospital.
Two welcome re-appearances in action- Stan Davies and Ron Linstead, both recovered from illness that has kept them out of running for some time.
David Davies, a City of London Policeman and son of Stan Davies, took part in the recent Barking - Southend 34 miles walk. In only his second appearance he finished 25th of the 139 starters.

A recent welcome visitor was Stan Davies, a good team man in his active days and a great club man. He is now settled in at his new home in Suffolk, near Haverhill.

Stan Davies (1914-2002) It is with much sadness that we have to announce the death of Stan Davies, who died on the 25th September 2002 from a heart attack, aged 88 years.
